name: Dollymount Strand
notes: Designated set-up/launch/land area at the wooden bridge end; stay 200 m from swimmers. Flat at low tide, best in southerlies.

name: Poolbeg (Shelly Banks)
notes: Between the power station and the port: flat shallow water ~4 h around high tide, long walk at low. Intermediate+.

name: Sutton – Burrow Beach
notes: Flat at mid to low tide in N–NE; tidal currents.

name: Portmarnock
notes: Velvet Strand: SE or N–NE winds, jumping conditions.

name: Rush South Beach
notes: Most powerful waves near Dublin in S–SW; any tide.

name: Bettystown
notes: S–SE cross-shore; strong currents.

name: Brittas Bay
notes: Clean cross-shore in S wind; busy in summer.

name: Rosslare Strand
notes: S–SE winds; rock groynes every ~300 m.

name: Lady's Island Lake
notes: Brackish lagoon, standing depth, butter flat; best in southerlies. Keep away from the tern islands and the northern reserve (summer breeding).

name: Duncannon
notes: Shallow flat water, kite school on the beach; choppy at high tide. W–S winds.

name: Tramore
notes: Open beach for all levels; lagoon behind the dunes at high tide. Surfers at the town end.

name: Garrylucas
notes: Cork's main kite beach (Garrettstown/Garrylucas), kite school; kickers in swell. SW best.

name: Inch Beach
notes: Wide sandy beach, flat to freeride.

name: Brandon Bay (Castlegregory)
notes: 17 km bay from Fermoyle to the Maharees: world-class waves in W–NW; gusty near the mountains. Experienced riders.

name: Maharees – Sandy Bay
notes: Tralee Bay side of the Castlegregory isthmus: sheltered flat water, Jamie Knox watersports centre.

name: Banna Strand
notes: Wide sandy beach, broad wind window; often choppy.

name: Lahinch
notes: Popular surf town: waves, experienced riders; W–SW cross-shore. Keep clear of surfers.

name: Galway – Silverstrand (Barna)
notes: Main Galway lesson spot; shallow flat lagoon at low tide. SW–W winds. Rusheen Bay next door is flat and sheltered.

name: Roundstone – Gurteen Bay
notes: Connemara: flat water, beginner friendly.

name: Louisburgh – Carrownisky
notes: 4 km swell magnet; small lake behind the beach for flat water in SW. High tide narrows the beach.

name: Achill – Keel
notes: Keel Strand for waves (gusty in NW), Keel Lough 100 m inland: knee-deep flat water, kite school, Battle of the Lake event.

name: Mulranny
notes: Clew Bay flat water, tide dependent.

name: Belmullet – Elly Bay
notes: Totally sheltered bay, flat water for beginners; Elly Beach on the open side for waves in S–SW.

name: Enniscrone
notes: Wide sandy bay, flat water, popular with kiters.

name: Rosses Point
notes: Nearest kite beach to Sligo, school; best mid tide, NW–SW. Crowded in summer.

name: Streedagh
notes: Freeride; flat lagoon at high tide for freestyle.

name: Bundoran – Tullan Strand
notes: Generally onshore, wide beach. Army range nearby: obey red flags.

name: Rossnowlagh
notes: Versatile, kite school; narrow at high tide.

name: Narin – Portnoo
notes: Sheltered 2 km beach, small waves, beginner friendly.

name: Magheraroarty
notes: Remote north-west beach popular with kite and windsurfers.

name: Dunfanaghy – Killahoey
notes: Open beach plus the flat Dunfanaghy lagoon behind it.

name: Downings
notes: Sheephaven Bay: sheltered water; Carrigart lagoon nearby.

name: Ballyliffin – Pollan Bay
notes: 3 km Inishowen beach, small waves.
